title: How can we picture doubling and tripling?
description: The numbers one, two, four, eight, sixteen are drawn as shapes that are doubled by joining two copies. The numbers one, three, nine, twenty seven are drawn by joining three copies.
teaching_notes: One idea: each shape is made of copies of the one before, joined together. Watch for students who draw a bigger shape without counting its dots or corners.

video_script.why: The child draws the numbers that double and triple as shapes made by joining copies of the shape before.
video_script.substitution: To get the next shape, join the right number of copies of the shape before.
video_script.anchor: two empty rows of frames, one for the numbers 1, 2, 4, 8 and one for the numbers 1, 3, 9, 27
video_script.payoff_line: Each shape is copies of the one before, joined together

final_answer.value: Powers of 2 (book, p.6): a point, a segment, a square, a cube, a 4-D cube for 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 (solutions add 32). Powers of 3: e.g. a dot, a triangle (3), three triangles joined in a row (9), three such rows joined (27).
final_answer.spoken: each shape is copies of the one before, joined together

hold_back: Each shape is copies of the one before, joined together
maths_rules: doubling: a point (1), a segment (2), a square (4), a cube (8), a four dimensional cube (16), each is two copies of the one before, joined
tripling: a dot (1), a triangle (3), three triangles joined in a row (9), three such rows joined (27)
video_script.design: One idea: join copies to get the next shape. Callback to the same dots made into different shapes. Wrong idea: none is broken. The two rows stay on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about two sequences of numbers.
<bookmark mark='first'/>One goes one, two, four, eight, and doubles each time.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The other goes one, three, nine, twenty seven, and triples each time.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can you draw a picture for each of them?

beats.on_screen: the two rows hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: one small shape, then two copies of it joined, then three copies of it joined

marks.join: the copies are joined into one bigger shape

narration: <bookmark mark='copy'/>A number that doubles is two copies of the one before.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Join the copies, and they make one bigger shape. A number that triples needs three copies.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the sequence one, two, four, eight, and the sequence one, three, nine, twenty seven.

marks.square: two segments join to make a square, and two squares join to make a cube

narration: <bookmark mark='point'/>Step one, doubling. A point is one, and two copies of it joined make a segment with two ends.
<bookmark mark='square'/>Two segments joined make a square with four corners. Two squares joined make a cube with eight corners.

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step two, one more shape. Two cubes joined make a four dimensional cube, and it has sixteen corners.

marks.dot: a dot appears, then three dots make a triangle

narration: <bookmark mark='dot'/>Step three, tripling. A dot is one, and three dots joined make a triangle.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>Three triangles joined in a row make nine, and three such rows joined make twenty seven.

marks.check: a tick appears beside sixteen and beside twenty seven

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check by counting. Two times eight is sixteen, and three times nine is twenty seven.
